thread:
anya: FYI seeing a regression on the TP + fused-attn path after the kernel-picker change in rfc/selector-v2 (commit d4f9c3b). Latency p95 jumped ~18% on 16-token avg seq. :frowning:
ricardo: Oof, do you have a repro script or a sample config we can quickly run?  :eyes:
anya: Yep. Repro command: `./bench --model llama-30b --tp=4 --seq=64 --batch=8 --use-fused-attn --kernel-selector=selector-v2 --kv-cache=sharded`
samir: Can you paste the profiler excerpt? nsys or perf would help.
anya: Pasted below — this is a 4-GPU run, TP=4. Notice the all-reduce tailing and long idle gaps on GPUs 2/3.
```
nsys profile summary:
  GPU 0 compute  1323ms  comm  142ms
  GPU 1 compute  1340ms  comm  138ms
  GPU 2 compute  1260ms  comm  310ms  <-- big
  GPU 3 compute  1285ms  comm  290ms  <-- big
  All-reduce avg 85ms, but variance high on last two ranks
```
marta: That smells like an imbalance from shard packing. Did selector-v2 change the qkv layout selection? selector-v2 picks `contiguous_kv` for some shapes which flips the all-gather pattern.
anya: Exactly. Before we used `interleaved_kv` for TP>1 when seq<128, now selector-v2 prefers `contiguous_kv` if fused-attn kernel reports lower local GEMM time. But the comm/compute overlap is worse for contiguous because our all-gather schedule doesn't chunk evenly.
ricardo: Hmm. So local kernel faster but exposes comm hotspots — classic compute/comm misalignment. Any KV-cache interaction? I remember sharded KV cache sizes varied across micro-batches.
anya: Yes. With sharded KV we pack variable-length prompts into micro-batches. Some shards end up with larger KV tensors (padding asymmetry). That increases the local kernel time and flips selector decision per-rank.
samir: That would make different ranks pick different qkv layout -> incompatible all-gather shapes -> we fallback to slower path or force scatter -> huge stalls.
marta: Is the fallback happening? Logs?
anya: Logs show: `kernel_picker: selected contiguous_kv on rank 2, interleaved_kv on rank 0` then later `comm: falling back to scalar-scatter due to shape mismatch`.
perf-bot: Regression alert: perf/regression/1876543201 created (p95 +18%).
ricardo: Quick mitigation options:
- revert selector-v2 change (safe but loses perf wins)
- add a global quorum step: require majority kernel choice or broadcast pick per-operator before launch
- modify selector to include a comm-cost estimate (simple model: comm_cost = allgather_bytes / bw + latency * n_chunks)
- normalize shard sizes / pad to uniform KV chunk size at micro-batch boundary
anya: I tried a small patch last night to broadcast the chosen layout from rank 0 to all ranks before fused kernel launch — that reduced p95 back to baseline in my toy run.
anya: Patch diff (pseudo):
```
# kernel_picker.py (pseudo)
choice = local_score(ops)
layout = comm.broadcast(choice, root=0)  # enforce uniform layout
launch_fused_attn(layout)
```
marta: Nice. Any downside? If root picks a suboptimal local kernel, we lose some compute perf, but avoid huge comm stalls. Might be acceptable as a safety heuristic.
samir: We should add a cost-aware selector instead of root-broadcast hack. Compute a score = local_time + estimated_comm_penalty. Estimated_comm_penalty = allgather_size / measured_bw + alpha * imbalance_var.
ricardo: Agree. Also add telemetry: expose per-rank kernel choice and comm times to the console so we can detect mismatches early.
anya: Created a minimal PR: https://git.company/repo/pulls/4821 — it has the broadcast fallback and logging. Benchmark on internal infra: 16-token p95: baseline 86ms, selector-v2 102ms, pr-4821 88ms.
marta: Can someone run pr-4821 on large-scale rig (tp=8, mixed seqs) to confirm? I can run later tonight.
samir: I'll draft a microbenchmark that forces asymmetric padding to reproduce reliably and include it in the CI perf suite.
ricardo: Long-term: update kernel profiler to report comm-weighted score and feed it into selector-v3. Owner: @samir for selector heuristics, @marta for infra runs, @anya for interim patch and validation. :thumbsup:
anya: I'll merge the broadcast patch to canary for now and open an issue to track selector-v3.
perf-bot: Canaries: deployment to canary-cluster started (deploy-777) :rocket:
marta: Thanks all — keep updates here. If someone sees a different regression pattern (e.g., all ranks choosing same layout but still high tail), ping infra so we can capture full nsys traces.
ricardo: Filing tracking ticket: PERF-1182 (linked to PR and nsys captures).
